A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same local data attribution framework and IIF algorithm. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated related work and renumbered experiments.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix C report original attribution analyses, filtering interventions, comparisons across six RL environments, and GPT-Neo detoxification experiments.

after.justification: The original empirical studies remain, with additional harmful-record case studies, Adam experiments, and statistical analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Remark 2 adds proposed algorithm-specific adaptations: changing per-sample loss gradients for TRPO/A3C and using a Bellman-error target with fresh validation rollouts for off-policy methods such as DQN. These are outlined extensions, not demonstrated implementations; the evaluated PPO/IIF and RLHF procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds Atari Pong as a harmful-record case study, illustrated in Figure 9. The original six RL environments and RealToxicityPrompts/Wiki-Toxic detoxification coverage remain. The additional BipedalWalker analysis uses an existing environment.

E2.justification: Appendix B.10 adds a reward-based difficulty-filtering comparator that removes records with extreme rewards and is reported to perform worse than random filtering. Standard PPO, random filtering, the two advantage heuristics, and the TD-error heuristic are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix B.7 adds Adam experiments for IIF and standard PPO on MiniGrid and LunarLander, whose existing main experiments use SGD. The previously specified benchmark budgets, evaluation metrics, and RLHF data-processing and testing protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 supplements the existing analyses with optimizer-sensitivity experiments, harmful-record case studies in BipedalWalker and Pong, and a difficulty-filtering failure analysis. Earlier single-round interventions, temporal analyses, filtering-percentage ablations, and RLHF target-function comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Figure 6 changes its reported averaging from three to five random seeds. Appendix B.8 newly reports t-based 95% confidence intervals for final performance gains on three environments. However, the added checklist still states that all experiments use three seeds, leaving an internal reporting inconsistency.

E6.justification: Figure 6 revises several summaries alongside its reported seed-count change; for example, MiniGrid SEpeak changes from 67.4% ± 4.4% to 61.7% ± 4.1%. New Adam results include SEpeak values of 13.3% ± 3.1% for MiniGrid and 62.2% ± 5.0% for LunarLander. Qualitative case-study and difficulty-filtering findings are added; the principal comparative conclusions and RLHF results remain.

T1.justification: The TracIn derivation, existing attribution objectives, graph-roughness definition, and efficiency-metric definitions retain their mathematical meaning. Explicit trajectory and prompt sampling notation clarifies existing objectives. Neither version provides formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: initiating local attribution for online RL, demonstrating three applications, and improving training through IIF across traditional RL and RLHF. Wording changes and additional supporting experiments do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of optimizer-dependent gains and attributes difficulty-filtering failure to removing helpful records alongside harmful ones. It expands applicability guidance for other RL algorithms and removes the earlier suggestion that attribution errors may compound exponentially. The stated optimizer and counterfactual limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly specifies LoRA fine-tuning with rank 16, alpha 32, and dropout 0.05, absent from v1's corresponding RLHF setup. This is additional documentation; the PDFs do not establish a change in the underlying experiment. Code access, hardware descriptions, and existing runtime breakdowns are retained.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the Ilyas et al. 2024 tutorial citation with the Deng et al. 2025 survey and adds references supporting LoRA, algorithm extensions, advantage-estimation issues, and difficulty filtering. Iyer et al. 2018 is removed. The main positioning relative to RL interpretability research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and challenge discussion receive limited rewriting, and Section 3.1 gains two explanatory remarks. Related work moves from Appendix A to Section 6, subsequent sections and appendices are renumbered, and a NeurIPS checklist is appended. Most prose and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 7 gains round-axis labels, and existing displays are repositioned. v2 adds the Pong montage, Adam learning curves, and Adam-metric and confidence-interval tables. Most earlier figures and tables retain their structure despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added Adam experiments and confidence intervals strengthen empirical support, while the LoRA settings fill a reproducibility gap. These are useful, limited improvements around an otherwise stable paper. Sparse experimental documentation for Pong and difficulty filtering, together with conflicting three-versus-five-seed statements, limits the strength of the revision.
